knowledge_point: Solving Cubic Equations With Leading Coefficients by Grouping
problem: Find all the real solutions to the equation $3{z}^{3}-{z}^{2}+27z-9=0.$
worked_solution:
We proceed to factor the left-hand side by grouping:

$$
\begin{aligned}3{z}^{3}-{z}^{2}+27z-9 & = \\ (3{z}^{3}-{z}^{2})+(27z-9) & = \\ {z}^{2}(3z-1)+9(3z-1) & = \\ (3z-1)\cdot {z}^{2}+(3z-1)\cdot 9 & = \\ (3z-1)({z}^{2}+9) & .\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we solve $(3z-1)({z}^{2}+9)=0$ by setting each factor equal to $0.$

- Setting the factor $(3z-1)$ equal to $0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3z-1 & =0 \\ 3z & =1 \\ z & =\frac{1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

- Setting the factor $({z}^{2}+9)$ equal to $0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{z}^{2}+9 & =0 \\ {z}^{2} & =-9.\end{aligned}
$$

Since a squared real number cannot be negative, the equation ${z}^{2}+9=0$ has no real solutions.

Therefore,  $z=\frac{1}{3}$ is the only real solution.
